text:
This looks like late 2010 or early 2011. Unemployment is 8.9%, which fits roughly November 2010 to February 2011. The fed funds rate is 0.13%, and the 10-year yield is 3.47%.

Headline CPI is 2.16% year over year, up 1.11 points over 3 months. That rise suggests an energy price jump. Core CPI is 1.09%, close to the low reached around late 2010 and early 2011.

Unemployment at 8.9% with a 3-month change of -0.9 means it was about 9.8% three months earlier. That points to February 2011, when unemployment was 8.9% (it was 9.8% in November 2010). Headline CPI in February 2011 was 2.1%, and core CPI was 1.1%, both matching.

The 10-year yield was around 3.4% to 3.5% at the end of February 2011. The VIX was about 17.7, which also fits. US large-cap equities returned +5.9% over 3 months and +17.3% over 6 months, again consistent with February 2011. The broad dollar was down about 5% year over year.
